requirements.evidence: routes/web.php:20-42 declares every contract route with the required methods/names/middleware (login/register guest, logout POST auth, home auth+verified, password.email throttle:6,1, verification.verify signed+throttled); Login.php:31-49 lowercases the e-mail, limits per e-mail+IP with auth.failed/auth.throttle, regenerates the session and redirectIntended(route('home')); Register.php:27-47 creates the user through RegisterUser (Registered event), logs in, regenerates and redirects; PasswordResetController.php:27-32,57-68 always flashes passwords.sent, rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset; EmailVerificationNotificationController.php:16-22 skips verified users and flashes status. Edge-case gap: Register.php:56 rejects mixed-case e-mails that login/reset accept. Requirement 9 for existing views cannot be confirmed from the diff (no existing view is modified).

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through app/Actions/RegisterUser.php:15-21; one-field inline validation in PasswordResetController.php:30-32 versus ResetPasswordRequest.php:32-38 for the larger rule set; reusable x-form-field component (form-field.blade.php:1-19) used by four forms; model already declares #[Fillable]/#[Hidden] (User.php:11-12); CHANGELOG.md updated. Deviation: Register.php:52-59 validates with a rules() method while the project pattern and the sibling Login.php:15-18 use #[Validate] attributes.

security.evidence: All client-writable inputs validated server-side (Login.php:15-18, Register.php:52-59) and re-checked with $this->validate(); rate limiting inside the actions (Login.php:32-41, Register.php:32-40); guest guard re-applied on Livewire update requests (Login.php:55-56, Register.php:65-66); signed+throttled verification route (routes/web.php:37-39); verification only marks the signed-in user via EmailVerificationRequest (VerifyEmailController.php:16-22); session regenerate on login/register (Login.php:47, Register.php:45); logout invalidates the session and rotates CSRF (LogoutController.php:18-19); remember_token rotated on reset (PasswordResetController.php:57-60); output always escaped with {{ }}, no secrets or debug output. No exploitable weakness found.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: LoginTest.php (case-insensitive e-mail, auth.failed, malformed e-mail, 5-attempt lock, per-e-mail scope, remember, signed-in user blocked, throttle key), RegisterTest.php (password-rule datasets, confirmed, unique, malformed, IP lockout, signed-in user blocked), PasswordResetTest.php (generic status, 6/min 429, token, remember_token, PasswordReset event, weak/mismatched password), EmailVerificationTest.php (valid, unsigned, tampered id, other user's link, guest, throttles, resend cases), HomeTest.php, LocalizationTest.php and ViewConventionsTest.php. Gaps: LogoutTest.php:19-28 never asserts the session id changed (invalidation), RegisterTest.php:29-49 never asserts session regeneration.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the existing User model and a new x-form-field component (form-field.blade.php) across login/register/forgot/reset, and keeps controllers thin. Some duplication: ensureGuest() is copy-pasted in Login.php:55-56 and Register.php:65-66, and the throttle-throw block repeats in Login.php:34-37 and Register.php:34-37; the layout also adds an unrequested CDN-Bulma fallback branch (app.blade.php:9-13).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with short docblocks (Login.php:23-26,43-49; PasswordResetController.php:21-28,52-57; RegisterUser.php:8-14), descriptive class/method names, consistent Laravel style, typed properties and no dead code, leftover debugging or commented-out code.

scope.evidence: The diff only touches auth components/controllers/requests/routes/views, lang/en/ui.php + lang/pt_BR/ui.php, .env.example, phpunit.xml, CHANGELOG.md and auth/localization tests; no SCSS/JS, Docker/nginx, notification theming or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The extra 'lowercase' rule rejects mixed-case addresses such as Ana@Example.com at registration even though Login.php:31 and ResetPasswordRequest.php:25 silently lowercase the same input, so the address works for login/reset but cannot be used to sign up; normalise with Str::lower instead of rejecting it.

issues.location: resources/views/welcome.blade.php and resources/views/bulma-test.blade.php (unchanged by the diff)
issues.explanation: Requirement 9 explicitly extends the route()/no-hardcoded-path rule to every existing view, but the diff modifies no existing view, so any href="/..." or action="/..." left in these files keeps the requirement unmet and would make the new all-views scan in tests/Feature/ViewConventionsTest.php:8 fail.

Register validates through a rules() method while the stated project pattern (and the sibling Login.php:15-18) uses #[Validate] attributes, leaving the two auth components with two different validation styles.
The logout test asserts the user is a guest and the CSRF token changed but never asserts the session id changed, so requirement 3's 'invalidates the session' is not actually covered.

The successful-registration test asserts user creation, verification mail and login but never asserts that the session was regenerated, so requirement 2's session-regeneration step has no regression test.
The throttle-error block and the ensureGuest() helper are duplicated almost verbatim between the two components, where a small shared trait/helper would keep a single definition.
The layout adds a CDN-Bulma fallback branch next to @vite that the task did not ask for, introducing a second styling path and an external dependency.
The scan only matches double-quoted href="/ and action="/ in Blade views, so single-quoted attributes and the redirect('/...') rule for controllers (also part of requirement 9) are not checked.

review.summary: The change implements the complete session-auth flow with Livewire full-page login/register components, logout, verified home, throttled password reset and signed e-mail verification, plus pt-BR-first translations and a broad Pest suite. It is well structured and has no exploitable security weakness; the remaining issues are small: registration rejects mixed-case e-mails that login accepts, the pre-existing views are not touched despite requirement 9, Register deviates from the #[Validate] pattern, and a couple of required session behaviours lack assertions.
